packets.title: org-core: refuse to start when ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED is on and the SIEM seal key is missing or invalid
packets.brief: Defect: with ORG_SIEM_DESTINATIONS_ENABLED=1 (or true) and ORG_CORE_SIEM_SEAL_KEY missing or invalid, org-core boots anyway. internal/http/server.go:74-86 only log.Printf's the NewSIEMSealerFromEnv error, so the SIEM routes stay mounted and answer 503 forever. The fix is boot validation. (1) In internal/http/siem_handlers.go, add an exported func ValidateSIEMDestinationsConfig(getenv func(string) string) error. When siemDestinationsEnabled(getenv) is false it returns nil and reads nothing else. When the flag is on it returns the error from orgcore.NewSIEMSealerFromEnv(getenv), wrapped with the flag name and never including the key value. (2) In cmd/server/main.go, call it right after the existing ValidateRequiredServiceCredentialRegistry check at the top of main(), using os.Getenv, and log.Fatalf("[org-core startup] SIEM destinations validation failed: %v", err) on error, the same way the credential-registry check fails. Keep NewServer's runtime fallback (log plus 503) untouched as defence in depth. Regression tests go in internal/http/siem_handlers_test.go and need a fake getenv: flag off with no key returns nil; flag "1" with no key returns an error; flag on with a malformed key (wrong length or non-base64) returns an error; flag on with a valid 32-byte base64 key returns nil; the error text never contains the key material. Must NOT change: the switch stays default off, and with it off the boot behaviour is identical (no new env read is required). Never log or print the seal key. The files are CRLF, so keep their line endings. Don't touch docker-compose.yml or the scripts.

packets.title: audit-verify CLI: verify the manifest signature and support a sub-range export
packets.brief: Defect: cmd/audit-verify/main.go only reads org_id, last_seq, last_row_hash, checkpoint, attestation and legacy_unchained_rows from the manifest (struct at main.go:97-104). It never checks the manifest signature that the server now produces. That signature is internal/store/compliance.go ComplianceManifest plus ManifestPayload at :254-277, signed via chain.KeyRing.SignPayload at internal/chain/sign.go:209, verifiable with KeyRing.VerifyPayload at sign.go:214. The CLI also always treats manifest last_seq as the chain head (main.go:192-194), so a sub-range export (the manifest's last_seq < head_seq, which the API produces for since/until) is reported broken or truncated_below_attestation even when the rows are intact. The fix: (1) Extend the CLI manifest struct with generated_at, first_seq, count, first_prev_hash, head_seq, head_hash, key_id and signature. Unknown fields are already allowed. (2) When key_id and signature are present, rebuild the payload with store.ManifestPayload (import internal/store and do not duplicate the byte format) and verify it with ring.VerifyPayload. On an invalid signature, exit 2 (broken) with a clear stderr line. On an unknown key id, exit 3 (unverifiable). With no signature, print "manifest: unsigned" in the report and keep today's exit behaviour for full-range exports. (3) Range mode applies when the manifest has head_seq > last_seq. Require a valid manifest signature, otherwise exit 3. Verify the rows from first_seq with FromSeq=first_seq and FromHash=first_prev_hash. Use Head={last_seq,last_row_hash} as the range end. Don't pass a newest attestation above last_seq: it would falsely report truncation. Check that the row count equals manifest count. Print that the range is anchored by the signed manifest rather than by an attestation. Never print a bare "verified" for a range that no signature anchors. Must NOT change: full-range verification results and exit codes for existing inputs (the current main_test.go cases must pass unchanged), the export row format, and anything under internal/store or internal/verifier. The files may be CRLF, so keep their line endings. Add table tests to cmd/audit-verify/main_test.go: signed full manifest verifies; tampered manifest field (for example last_seq or legacy count) gives exit 2; unknown key id gives exit 3; signed sub-range verifies (exit 0) where the old code reported broken; unsigned sub-range gives exit 3; existing unsigned full manifest is unchanged.

packets.title: audit-core verifier loop: a saved cursor above the chain head (after a restore) must reset, not report head_behind_chain
packets.brief: Defect: after audit tables are restored from an older copy, audit_chain_verifications.verified_through_seq can exceed the restored head. verifier.verifyOrg (internal/verifier/verifier.go:580-629) resumes from st.ThroughSeq (:593-594). Verify then reads no rows, so rangeEnd = FromSeq-1 > Head.Seq, and it returns broken/head_behind_chain (:380-381) with no real defect. Two things keep it there: the broken branch keeps the cursor (:605-609), and :620 only ever raises ThroughSeq, so every later pass repeats the false break. The fix, inside verifyOrg only: when the report is broken with ReasonHeadBehindChain and the run resumed from a stored cursor (opts.FromSeq > 0), log a warning (org id and the two sequence numbers only) and re-run once from the trust base (Options with FromSeq/FromHash zero and the same MaxRows). Use that report from then on. On a non-broken result, when the run started from the trust base and rep.Complete, set next.ThroughSeq/ThroughHash to rep's values even if they are lower than st.ThroughSeq, so the stale cursor is replaced. Keep the existing raise-only rule for incremental runs. A genuine head_behind_chain (rows beyond the head) must still end broken after the re-run, and verifyFailures must be incremented exactly once per pass. Regression tests go in internal/verifier/verifier_test.go using the existing fakeSource (around :600-720): the state has ThroughSeq above the fake head, a clean chain ends verified with ThroughSeq reset to the head and no failure counted, and a chain whose rows really extend past the head still ends broken with head_behind_chain and counts one failure. Must NOT change: the Verify() rules, the store package, the switches, or the broken-chain cursor behaviour for every other reason. The files may be CRLF, so keep their line endings.

packets.title: model-gateway: stage Ask-turn files into code_interpreter, type the vision_unsupported refusal, and filter the vision check by provider
packets.brief:
Three confirmed gaps in model-gateway's Ask (non-agentic) stream path, all in sse.rs.

(1) Files are accepted, then dropped. With CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED=true, attachment_policy.rs:174/264/296 accepts kind:"file" and declares modes.sandbox_files=true. But nothing calls turn_attachments::sandbox_staging_enabled() (turn_attachments.rs:32), and sse.rs:2913 calls tool_loop::run_tool_rounds_for_model. That wrapper (tool_loop.rs:6782-6812) always passes ValidatedAttachments::none(), so files validate and are silently ignored. Fix: in invoke_stream_sse, before any durable run is prepared (next to the image_parts/do_attachments admission at sse.rs:1543-1617, and only when the turn is not agentic), build `crate::turn_attachments::ValidatedAttachments::from_invoke(&req.attachments, crate::turn_attachments::sandbox_staging_enabled(), effective_zdr || retention_class.is_some())`. On Err(refusal), return error_stream(&request_id, refusal.code.as_str(), &refusal.message, false), the same as the Do path at sse.rs:1601-1611. Move the value into the spawned task. At sse.rs:2913, call crate::tool_loop::run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments(..., &staged, &image_parts) instead. Files must never be dropped silently: when staged is non-empty and the turn offers no code_interpreter tool (tool_defs empty, or no tool named code_interpreter), end the turn with a typed attachment refusal (AttachmentCode::MediaUnsupported, retryable false), not a silent drop. Put that check before the run is prepared if tool_defs is known there, otherwise as a prepared failure.

(2) vision_unsupported reads as an outage. inference-core refuses an image turn with FAILED_PRECONDITION plus the trailer x-mp-provider-error=vision_unsupported (inference-core grpc.rs:1700/1837). The gateway's direct-inference failure arm at sse.rs:7650-7671 only knows subscription failures and model_entitlement, so the refusal becomes code model_plane_unavailable with retryable:true, and terminal_code stays inference_unavailable (sse.rs:7611-7613). Fix: add a small helper in sse.rs that reads the trailer (crate::compaction::PROVIDER_ERROR_KIND_TRAILER) and recognises exactly "vision_unsupported". Use it to emit ChatEvent::Error { code: "vision_unsupported", message: a fixed sentence (the selected model cannot read images; pick a model that reads images or remove the image), retryable: false }, and use the same code as the terminal code. Do not change any other mapping.

(3) The vision check ignores the picked provider. The vision-capability check at sse.rs:1560-1566 sends ListModelsRequest::default(). Org model-access policy is already applied by inference-core (grpc.rs:518-525 filters chat models by the caller's principal), but the user's picked provider is not, so for a Verevon mode any listed vision model counts. Fix: set ListModelsRequest.provider to the turn's provider hint when one is non-empty (default otherwise). Check that the variable is in scope at that point; if it is not, derive it the same way the rest of the handler does.

Must NOT change: CHAT_SANDBOX_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED, CHAT_VISION_AS_PARTS_ENABLED and CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED stay default off; with the sandbox switch off, from_invoke returns none() and behaviour is byte-identical; a ZDR or waived turn never stages a file (refused); the Do-path admission is unchanged; no bytes or file names are logged (counts and sizes only, as turn_attachments.rs does); context_recovery_contract.rs must keep finding run_tool_rounds_for_model_with_attachments. Do not edit attachment_policy.rs, vision_parts.rs or tool_loop.rs (other packets own them). Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Regression tests in sse.rs's test module:
(a) A pure helper test: switch on with a file attachment yields a non-empty ValidatedAttachments; switch off yields empty; ZDR or waived yields a refusal.
(b) The trailer helper maps a Status with x-mp-provider-error=vision_unsupported to code vision_unsupported, retryable false; another kind and a missing trailer map to None.
(c) The ListModelsRequest builder carries the provider hint when set and is the default when empty.

packets.title: execution-core: children get no attached files, RunInputs lives as long as the run, resumed runs refuse with attachments_expired
packets.brief:
Three confirmed defects in how execution-core holds a Do run's attached files (all behind CHAT_DO_ATTACHMENTS_ENABLED, which stays default off).

(1) Children inherit the parent's files. The code_interpreter arm of execute_step_inner reads `crate::run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id)` with no depth check (runtime_loop/mod.rs:893). A delegated child runs with the parent's run_id (agent.rs:5360, `req: parent.req`), so the child's code_interpreter stages the parent's attachments/. The plan says children do not inherit attachments, and the existing test children_do_not_inherit_attachments (agent.rs:26826) covers only images and the note. Fix: add a `read_run_inputs: bool` parameter to execute_step_with_result_handles and execute_step_inner (mod.rs:583/647). The agent loop call at agent.rs:3984 passes `ctx.depth == 0`. Every other caller (execute_step, execute_step_with_browser_grant, execute_step_with_subagent, and the test at mod.rs:2375) passes true, so their behaviour is identical. At mod.rs:893 write it as `let ro_inputs = if read_run_inputs { crate::run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id) } else { None };` so the literal `run_inputs::global().get(org_id, run_id)` that tests/cross_service_loop_contract.rs:463/545 pins is still present.

(2) The registry sweeps a live run's files. run_inputs.rs sweeps every entry older than DEFAULT_TTL (15 min, run_inputs.rs:32 and 267-278) on the next registration, even while the run's guard is alive, so a Do run longer than 15 minutes loses its files mid-run. Fix: store a per-entry expiry. Add `register_until(org_id, run_id, attachments, ttl: Duration)` and keep `register` as `register_until(.., self.ttl)`, so grpc.rs:1045 (ExecuteStep) is unchanged. The sweep compares against each entry's own expiry. register_run_inputs (agent.rs:2338, called at agent.rs:1609 inside the driver that has `deadline: RunDeadline`) passes the run deadline's remaining time from deadline.remaining_at(Instant::now()), never less than the default 15 min, and with a hard ceiling (for example 24 h) when the deadline has no limit, so a leaked guard is still evicted.

(3) A resumed run is told about files it no longer has. A parked, in-place-resumed or continuation Do run loses its files, because the guard lives only inside run_agent. The restored or parked messages (agent.rs:2531-2545) still hold the sandbox note that says attachments/ exists. The plan (build plan WS08-S6 row) says a resumed Do run re-requests attachments, with refusal reason `attachments_expired`, rather than persisting them. Fix:
- In mp-contracts attachments.rs, add `pub const ATTACHMENTS_EXPIRED: &str = "attachments_expired";` and `pub fn is_sandbox_note(content: &str) -> bool`, which matches the fixed first sentence that sandbox_note writes.
- In run_rounds, on the restored and parked branches, when any restored message is a system message for which is_sandbox_note is true and the request carries no file attachments (split_attachments(&req.attachments).0 is empty), return Err(tonic::Status::failed_precondition(ATTACHMENTS_EXPIRED)) before the first inference round. Do this before any tool runs.
- Check that this refusal does not consume a granted approval a second time and leaves the run as the other resume refusals do. If the refusal can only be raised after the approval is consumed, raise it there and record that in a comment.

Must NOT change: the switch stays default off; a run without attachments behaves byte-identically (no note, nothing registered, no refusal); ZDR runs never carry files; no bytes or names are logged; register's public behaviour for ExecuteStep is unchanged. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Tests to add:
(a) In agent.rs: a child that calls code_interpreter sees no ro_inputs (extend children_do_not_inherit_attachments, or add a_child_code_interpreter_step_sees_no_attached_files, asserting the registry lookup is skipped at depth 1).
(b) In run_inputs.rs: an entry registered with a long TTL survives a sweep_at(now + 16 min), and a default entry does not.
(c) In agent.rs: an in-place or parked resume whose restored messages hold the sandbox note, with no attachments on the request, fails with attachments_expired; the same resume without the note proceeds.
(d) In mp-contracts: is_sandbox_note is true for sandbox_note output and false for arbitrary text.

packets.title: execution-core code_interpreter: do not chmod through a planted attachments symlink in a persistent Space root
packets.brief:
code_interpreter.rs stages attached files into <root>/attachments. StagedInputs::stage (code_interpreter.rs:686-725) first calls remove_staged_dir(root/attachments) (line 706). remove_staged_dir (lines 736-745) calls set_mode(dir, 0o755), which is std::fs::set_permissions and follows symlinks, then remove_dir_all. In a persistent Space root (run_in_root with persistent=true, line 577; reached from the Do-attachments path), a program from an earlier call of the same run can plant `attachments` as a symlink to a host path. The next staging call then chmods the target as the execution-core user.

Fix remove_staged_dir: first read std::fs::symlink_metadata(dir).
- NotFound: return quietly.
- A symlink or any non-directory: std::fs::remove_file it, with no chmod.
- A real directory: chmod and remove as today.
Also make Drop for StagedInputs and the create_dir path safe: create_dir must fail rather than follow a symlink that reappears (it already does on unix, since create_dir does not follow a final symlink; keep it so). Do not change the reserved-name rule (files_in may not be named attachments, line 288).

Must NOT change: the ephemeral path; read-only modes 0o444/0o555; staging is still refused where the OS sandbox is unavailable; nothing logs file content. Files are CRLF: preserve line endings.

Tests to add, in code_interpreter.rs tests and #[cfg(unix)] because they need symlinks and modes:
(a) remove_staged_dir on a symlink `attachments` that points to a directory with mode 0o500: the link is removed and the target's mode is unchanged.
(b) remove_staged_dir on a regular file named attachments removes it.
(c) remove_staged_dir on a staged read-only directory removes it.
(d) A persistent-root test (D1-608): two successive stagings into the same root both succeed, the second after a leftover attachments directory.

packets.title: inference-core: effort ceilings also bound the legacy thinking budget, and the org policy max_effort is applied at the PEP (covers the agentic path)
packets.brief:
Two effort ceilings in inference-core leave holes.

(1) Budget clamp, legacy budget (D1-032/033). In `apps/Model Plane/rust/services/inference-core/src/provider/fallback.rs`, `resolve_intent` (around lines 1079-1098) clamps only `rewritten.reasoning_effort` (an `Option<effort::Level>`) to `decision.effort_cap` when `effort::budget_clamp_enabled()` (env `INFERENCE_CORE_EFFORT_BUDGET_CLAMP`, only the literal `true`). The first half of the row (reasoning_effort never reaching InferRequest) is fixed: model-gateway now sets it (`thinking.rs`, `sse.rs:3068`, `http_routes.rs:10519`) and `grpc.rs:1230` maps it. What is still wrong: when `reasoning_effort` is `None` (gateway ladder switch `MODEL_GATEWAY_EFFORT_LADDER` off), the request carries the legacy `thinking_budget_tokens` and that is never clamped, so an exhausted-budget org still spends the full legacy budget. Fix: when the clamp is on and `decision.effort_cap` is `Some(cap)` and `reasoning_effort` is `None` and `thinking_budget_tokens > 0`, set `thinking_budget_tokens = min(thinking_budget_tokens, effort::allowance(cap))` and log it with the same content-free `clamped = true` info line. Put the arithmetic in a small pure helper in `provider/effort.rs` (e.g. `pub fn cap_legacy_budget(budget: i32, cap: Option<Level>) -> i32`: never raises, `None` cap and `budget <= 0` return the input unchanged) so it is unit-testable.

(2) Org policy max_effort is not applied at the PEP (D1-499). Only model-gateway clamps the effort to the policy's `max_effort` (`model_access.rs` `Admitted::clamp_effort`, called from `sse.rs:1197` and `http_routes.rs:10474`). execution-core's agent loop calls inference-core directly (RunAgentRequest path), so a role capped at e.g. `low` can still run a deep agent loop. inference-core is the enforcement point and already carries the caller's entitlement on `InferRequest.access` (`Option<Arc<RequestAccess>>`, set by `with_access` in grpc.rs). Fix in fallback.rs: add one helper applied in BOTH `infer_with_response_cache` (after `pinned_model`/`resolve_intent`, line ~1303-1309) and `infer_stream` (line ~1721-1723), BEFORE the response-cache lookup (the cache key hashes the effort level): when `req.access` is `Some(access)` and `access.enforced()` and the resolved policy has a non-empty `max_effort` (use `access.resolved().clamp_effort(name)` from `mp_contracts::model_entitlement::ResolvedAccess`, or `Level::from_name` + `effort::clamp_to_cap`), lower `reasoning_effort` to the ceiling, and when `reasoning_effort` is `None` cap `thinking_budget_tokens` with the same `cap_legacy_budget` helper. Clamp down only, never up; an unknown ceiling name leaves the request alone (it is validated at write time by org-core). Since `req` is `&InferRequest`, clone only when a change is needed.

Must NOT change: with `INFERENCE_CORE_EFFORT_BUDGET_CLAMP` unset and `MODEL_ENTITLEMENT_MODE` off/shadow the request is byte-identical to today (no clamp, no clone visible in behaviour); a service principal (access None / exempt) is never clamped; no content in logs (ids, level names, numbers only). Keep the files' existing line endings (check CRLF vs LF before editing).

Regression tests (unit, in the files' existing `#[cfg(test)]` modules): effort.rs `cap_legacy_budget` cases (4096 capped to 1024 by Low, 512 under Low unchanged, 0 and negative unchanged, None cap unchanged); fallback.rs: a request with `access` enforced and a policy max_effort `low` and `reasoning_effort = Some(High)` reaches the provider (use the existing mock provider pattern in fallback.rs tests, e.g. the tests near `preserves_explicitly_pinned_model` / `the_streaming_path_honors_a_pinned_model`) with `Low`; the same with `reasoning_effort = None, thinking_budget_tokens = 4096` reaches it with 1024; the same request under shadow (not enforced) reaches it unchanged; one streaming-path case.

packets.brief:
Context: session-core's crash park (WS03-S8, switch SESSION_CORE_CRASH_PARK_ENABLED, default off) re-seals a dead loop's last ROUND fold as a park and refuses any fold that lacks the route markers: session-core/src/loop_checkpoint.rs:793-799 returns `route_unrecorded` when `route_model_in`, `route_connection_in` or `child_ceiling_in` (non-zero) is missing, and crash_park_fold (loop_checkpoint.rs:814-828) takes the next park number from `parks_in(fold)`.

Defect 1 (D1-543/D1-549): execution-core writes the four markers (lf::EXT_PARKS, EXT_ROUTE_MODEL, EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION, EXT_CHILD_CEILING) only in `park::park_fold` (runtime_loop/park.rs:368-395, doc comment says 'written here and nowhere else'). The round fold built at runtime_loop/agent.rs ~4348-4369 (`fold::build_fold(...)` then `folds.save_round(fold)`) carries none, so with the crash-park switch on every crash park is refused as route_unrecorded. Fix: when (and only when) the loop's `park_gate.run_parkable` is true (agent.rs ~2648, ParkGate), add the four markers to the round fold before `save_round`: EXT_PARKS = park_gate.parks_so_far (the resumed run's count from the claimed fold, so the park cap holds across crash resumes; a fresh loop writes 0), EXT_ROUTE_MODEL = ctx.route.model(), EXT_ROUTE_CONNECTION = ctx.route.subscription_connection_id(), EXT_CHILD_CEILING = the same child ceiling value the park site (ParkSite.child_ceiling) uses. Factor one helper in park.rs (e.g. `insert_route_markers(fold: &mut LoopFoldV1, site/route values, parks: u32)`) and make park_fold use it too, so both folds write identical keys; update the park.rs doc comment. Never write the markers on a non-parkable run: run_parkable already excludes approval continuations (holds_release), client/MCP-tool runs (tools_derivable false), ZDR, waived, Space, non-root and unpinned runs - reuse that one decision, do not add a second. Never write them on pre_effect, pause, fence or tombstone folds. Never copy session-core's `thread_watermark` extension into any executor-written fold (build_fold must keep starting from a fresh extensions map; session-core stamps round folds itself).

Defect 2 (D1-544, zombie loop): FoldWriter::apply (runtime_loop/fold.rs:1034-1051) marks the writer Failed on SaveError::Stale/Closed, and the loop only holds effectful calls afterwards (agent.rs ~3654-3672); it keeps running read-only rounds and can append a final answer. When session-core crash parks a loop that was merely slow, the live loop's next save goes stale and a continuation can run beside it, so two loops answer one run. Fix: for a run_parkable loop only, when a round/pre-effect save returns Stale or Closed (expose a narrow accessor on FoldWriter such as `lost_fence() -> bool` that is true only for State::Failed(SaveError::Stale|SaveError::Closed), not for Refused), stop the loop at that point before any further inference, append, receipt or tool dispatch, and end the RunAgent call with a typed status (e.g. Status::aborted("loop_checkpoint_superseded")) without reporting an answer. Check after save_round at the end of a round and wherever save_pre_effect returns Hold. Non-parkable runs must keep today's behaviour exactly (held effects, loop continues).

Must not change: behaviour with parking off or the crash-park switch off is byte-identical (markers only when run_parkable, which is false with parking off); no new switch; ZDR/waived runs never write folds; files are CRLF in this worktree - preserve line endings.

The docstring admits it ("A rename that moves a file out of the count is not detected").

Fix: in compare_with_base, for each path in the BASE baseline that is no longer a counted file now (`counts.get(path) is None`), ask git for renames between the base and the tree being checked: `git diff --name-status -z -M <base_ref>` against the working tree (or `<base_ref> <ref>` when --ref is given). If the path was renamed (R status) to a destination that is not counted (not in counts, or counts[dest] is None as generated), report `<old>: renamed to <new>, which is not counted; a baselined file cannot leave the count by moving`. A destination that IS counted is handled by the existing rules (it is over the cap with no ceiling unless the baseline moves with it — and a new entry for it must not exceed the old ceiling: treat a renamed entry's allowance as the old path's ceiling in the raise check). A plain deletion (D) stays allowed. Update the module docstring sentence accordingly.

Tests in scripts/tests/test_size_ratchet.py (use the existing Repo helper): a baselined file git-mv'ed into gen/ fails with --base-ref; renamed to an uncounted suffix fails; renamed to another counted path with its ceiling carried over passes; deleted outright passes.

Must NOT change: CAP, counted suffixes, --update/--init behaviour, exit codes.
